extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, patent examiners, and judges handling patent appeals/interferences
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing appeals from the Commissioner of Patents, interference proceedings, and the taking/transmission of evidence under the Acts of 1836 and 1839 as explained in Judge Cranch's decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship requirement (6th section)
rubrics_metrics.description: By the sixth section of the act, the applicant must be the inventor. One of three joint inventors cannot with propriety be called the inventor; and if he applies for the patent, the Commissioner is bound to refuse it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant is not the sole inventor (e.g., there are joint inventors), the Commissioner has authority to withhold the grant. The opinion emphasizes that an applicant who falsely claims sole inventorship would be implying perjury if he acknowledged joint inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use/time bar (two-year public use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suffering the machine to be in public use for more than two years before application for a patent may cause the inventor to lose his right to a patent (the statute uses the words 'public use').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge Cranch originally relied on this ground but later deemed it beyond the points stated in the reasons of appeal and withdrew that part of his opinion as extra-judicial. The standard itself remains stated as a bar under the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of judicial review limited to reasons of appeal (11th sec. / act of 1839)
rubrics_metrics.description: The judge's revision shall be confined to the points involved in the reasons of appeal; he is to 'hear and determine such appeals' but to revise only in respect to the points in the reasons of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Commissioner did not err on those points, his decision on them must be affirmed even if the judge thinks the patent ought to have been granted on other grounds. The judge's decision governs further proceedings of the Commissioner only as to the points involved in the reasons of appeal; the Commissioner may still reject on other untouched grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of appeal (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal under the patent laws can be taken only from a rejection of an application by the Commissioner; no appeal is generally given from the granting of a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rationale: a rejected applicant has no other remedy to obtain a patent, whereas a patentee has ordinary judicial remedies if a patent is erroneously granted to another. Thus appeals are designed to correct refusals, not grants (except as provided elsewhere, e.g., §8 interference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference/priority appeals (§8 of 1836 act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application would, in the opinion of the Commissioner, interfere with any other pending application or an unexpired patent, the Commissioner must give notice to the applicant or patentee; if dissatisfied, either (applicants) may appeal on the like terms and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The judge's jurisdiction under §8 is limited to determining 'which or whether either of the applicants is entitled to receive a patent as prayed for.' The provision contemplates contending applicants; a patentee (one who already has a patent) is not generally an 'applicant' entitled to such an appeal except in the interference context described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner and judge have special, limited statutory powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The powers and jurisdiction given to the board of examiners and to the judge are special and limited and must be construed and exercised strictly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authorities can only decide what the statutes expressly authorize; statutory language and purposes (e.g., that appeals are to correct refusals) should govern interpretation. This limits both proceedings and remedies available within the patent office/appeal process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-issuance limits on Commissioner's authority (13th section exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the patent has issued, the jurisdiction of the Commissioner is exhausted, except in the case provided for in the 13th section where the patent is inoperative or invalid by reason of a defective or insufficient description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudications by the Commissioner or the Judge have no effect on an issued patent as to the rights of the parties unless the decision is against the applicant (and statutory appeals apply). A patentee whose patent is valid is not affected by later office proceedings; if invalid, the patentee has no right to complain in that administrative setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for injured patentee (§16 / equity and law)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 16th section provides remedies where a patent is refused or where there are interfering patents; a patentee may bring a bill in equity (or an action at law for infringement) to adjudicate validity or void patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These remedies are the ordinary tribunals' mechanisms to correct erroneously granted patents. The statute provides that where a patent is granted to another, the first patentee may seek equity to have the second patent adjudged void or proceed at law for infringement, using judicial processes including oaths and testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of examiners review when specifications/claim modified (7th section)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the specification and claim shall not have been so modified as, in the opinion of the Commissioner, shall entitle the applicant to a patent, he may on appeal, and upon request in writing, have the decision of a board of examiners who may reverse the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affords an administrative review mechanism when the Commissioner thinks modifications might entitle the applicant to a patent; it is part of the internal remedial structure distinct from judicial appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's duty to give notice of interference and to file grounds in writing (8th and 11th sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall give notice when an application interferes with another pending application or unexpired patent, and must lay before the judge all original papers and evidence together with the grounds of his decision fully set forth in writing touching all points involved in the reasons of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper notification and written grounds are prerequisites to appeal and judicial revision; the administrative record must present the points the judge is to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-taking and transmission rules (Patent Office circular / rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules: (1) All statements, declarations, evidence shall be in writing, setting forth minutely and particularly the points at issue, and verified by oath or affirmation. (2) All such material shall be filed in the Patent Office by the parties before the day of hearing. (3) Before taking depositions, notice of time/place must be given the opposite party so they may cross-examine; proof of service to be attached. (4) No evidence touching the matter at issue will be considered on the day of hearing which was not taken and filed in compliance with these rules, except where inability to procure testimony is shown by notice received ten days prior. (5) All evidence shall be sealed and transmitted to the Commissioner by the persons before whom it was taken, and so certified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedural requirements govern contested cases: form (writing and oath), timing (filed before hearing), adversarial opportunity (notice and cross-examination), transmission formalities (sealed, certified), and a narrow exception for inability to procure witnesses with timely notice. Failure to comply may render depositions not amenable to consideration on the day set, though the Commissioner may postpone to enable cure in the interests of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's discretion to postpone hearing to cure informality or further justice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may postpone a hearing to enable a party to cure an informality in transmission of evidence or, having due regard to the public interest, postpone to further the ends of justice and give both parties opportunity to procure further testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 4th rule's prohibition is against considering informally transmitted evidence 'upon the day of hearing' as evidence, not against the Commissioner reading or ascertaining its contents for other administrative purposes. Postponement without the applicant's consent is defended where necessary to serve justice and public interest; objections to insufficient notice for cross-examination should generally be raised at trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and protest obligations regarding evidentiary objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Objections relating to the insufficiency of notice to permit cross-examination or other procedural infirmities should be made at the time of trial; failure to object then may forfeit the right to complain on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner noted that some objections did not arise at trial and 'should have then been made' — indicating a duty to timely protest procedural shortcomings to preserve appellate review of those procedural complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of judge's affirmance/ reversal limited to appealed points
rubrics_metrics.description: If the judge affirms or reverses the Commissioner's decision on the points in the reasons of appeal, that decision only governs subsequent proceedings of the Commissioner insofar as those points involved the merits; other untouched sufficient reasons may still support rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A judge's reversal on the limited points does not automatically grant a patent if other statutory objections not involved in the appeal remain; conversely, affirmation on appealed points leaves other Commissioner objections intact.
